page.layout: One printed page. Centred title block at the top, then section I (a verse stanza with a decorative initial V), an attribution, section II (verse), and the catchword at the lower right. No marginal notes. The fragments at the right edge belong to the neighbouring page and are left out.

main_text.head: In commendationem ELEGANTISSIMI OPERIS, à CL.V. D. JOHANNE STEKIO, IC. EDITI.

p.i: VERBA nihil scire est legum, si sensus aberrat; Haec est Juridici regula prima chori. Tu verba, & legum sensum bene perspicis; ergo Juristas inter tu mihi primus eris.

main_text.p: M. LUDOVICUS LUCIUS, Basileae Organi Aristotelici Professor.

p.i: SUMMUS Deorum Rex, & aequus arbiter, Quum condidisset Orbis axes maximi, Distare Divos censuit certis notis. Hinc, Ipse, fulmen horridum manu gerit; Hinc, Mars coruscâ cassíde obnubit caput; Virgam, hinc, colubris implicat Cyllenius; Hinc, quisq; signa fert sibi dati offici. Astraea (nostris exulat quae finibus)

page.notes: The large initial V is a woodcut ornament joined to the first word. Ornamental rules above and below the section headings are not text. The small-capital words are rendered in capitals. Some letters in the verse are faint but read with reasonable certainty.
